name: Local First Tools
tagline: 2885+ single-file, offline-first web tools. Build logs, demos, and things that run entirely in your browser.
_note: This channel lives inside the localFirstTools repo, not inside rapp-vision. It is the proof that a channel can be hosted anywhere: RAPP Vision resolves every path below against THIS file's URL. The live scenes below drive the real apps in this same repo.

videos.title: LIVE REPLAY: ten apps, driven in real time — no video file
videos.description:
This entry has no video. It is a script.

Instead of streaming a pre-rendered MP4, RAPP Vision loads each real application in an iframe and replays the recorded interactions against it on a clock — the same keystrokes and clicks that produced the video, executed live. Play, pause and seek work as normal.

The whole thing is a few kilobytes of JSON against 26 MB of video, and because the app is genuinely running you can pause at any point and take over.

This is only possible because these are single-file, offline-first apps served from the same origin. The static video is still published alongside it — both forms, same story.

live.note: Scenes run in order. Each drives a real app in an iframe.

lower.title: Apex Driving Simulator
lower.bug: Track spline had a 7.28° kink at the loop seam

scenes._drive: Recorded in-situ by critic/tune2.mjs: a closed-loop controller drove the real sim inside this very player, and its key transitions were captured as a plain open-loop schedule.
scenes._note: Addressed by id, not label: #btnCam renames itself Chase/Cockpit/Hood as it cycles. Times are measured from the moment #startBtn becomes clickable, not from scene start. The throttle burst is deliberately short: this sim integrates physics per frame, so a longer pull reached 11.7 m/s on one run and 24.7 m/s on the next, and the fast one hit a barrier. A live scene must only ask for what is robust to timing.
